topStories.headline: Lake Merced Trail Fully Reopens on Skyline Boulevard After Summer Construction
topStories.dek: SF Rec & Park says the path along Skyline Blvd is open again, with new ADA upgrades and fitness stations still to come.
topStories.body:
Walkers, runners, and cyclists circling Lake Merced got good news this week: the trail segment along Skyline Boulevard is once again open after a construction closure that had been in place through late June. San Francisco Recreation and Parks posted the update on September 4, confirming that the Skyline Blvd pathway is now accessible to the public without detours.

The reopening is part of the larger Lake Merced Trail Improvement Project. According to the Rec & Park notice, work on the northern section of the lake is ongoing — construction activities are expected to continue through the end of the year — but no further significant closures or pedestrian detours are anticipated as part of the project.

When complete, the improvements will include a fully ADA-compliant asphalt path reconstructed from Harding Park Road to the Sunset Circle parking lot, six new ADA parking spaces in that lot, a softer stabilized-soil path for runners alongside the paved trail, and replacement of existing fitness stations with new adult exercise equipment. Questions can be directed to the project manager at omar.davis@sfgov.org.

topStories.headline: Empire Theater Project Grows to 172 Units and 12 Stories — and May Skip Public Hearings
topStories.dek: DM Development's revised plan for the shuttered West Portal theater has more than doubled in size, enabled by state streamlining laws and Mayor Lurie's Family Zoning changes.
topStories.body:
The proposed redevelopment of the shuttered Empire Theater at 85 West Portal Avenue has grown dramatically since it was first reported earlier this year. Developer DM Development, acting for owner Empire West Portal LLC, has filed revised plans that would replace the vacant theater and an adjacent Goodwill and Supercuts building with a 12-story, 172-unit mixed-use complex — up from the original nine-story, 64-unit proposal announced in January.

The expansion was made possible in part by Mayor Daniel Lurie's 'Family Zoning' changes and the acquisition of the neighboring property at 61 West Portal Avenue. The revised plan calls for 172 rental apartments, including 26 affordable units — half targeting very-low-income households and half targeting moderate-income families — plus approximately 7,000 square feet of ground-floor retail.

Critically for neighbors hoping to weigh in, the development is invoking two state laws designed to streamline housing approvals, meaning it could move forward without public hearings or votes. A state density-bonus program is also helping push the building's permitted height higher. The project is widely expected to face legal challenges from neighborhood groups, following a pattern seen in similar upzoning battles elsewhere in the city.

San Francisco is under pressure to permit 82,000 new homes by 2031 but has produced roughly 6,500 so far, according to the SF Chronicle. The Empire Theater site has been vacant since Cinemark closed the theater in early 2021.

topStories.headline: SFSU Opens Fall Semester With Constitution Day Conference and GatorFest Events
topStories.dek: San Francisco State University's two-day Constitution and Citizenship Day conference runs September 16–17, while GatorFest programming continues through November.
topStories.body:
San Francisco State University is heading into a busy stretch of campus programming this week. The university's annual 'Rights and Wrongs: A Constitution and Citizenship Day Conference' is scheduled for Wednesday, September 16, and Thursday, September 17, marking a national holiday that commemorates the signing of the U.S. Constitution in 1787. According to the SFSU Campus Memo published September 8, the conference will include a keynote by Lori Fogarty, director of the Oakland Library, on the topic of 'Museums and the Fullness of History,' along with faculty and student panels and pop-up exhibits from the Sutro Library.

Meanwhile, GatorFest 2026 — the university's multi-month welcome program for new and returning students — is continuing its run of campus events. The Campus Memo notes that GatorFest won't end now that classes have begun, with events continuing through Friday, November 20. Upcoming offerings include two weeks of 'Meet the Org' events on Malcolm X Plaza, Sports Club Week with a pep rally and field day, and Greek life information sessions. GatorFest also extends off campus, with a September outing to cheer on the San Francisco Giants.

SFSU began the fall semester the week of August 21, welcoming new and returning Gators to the 1600 Holloway Avenue campus.

moreNews.headline: Stonestown Galleria Now Opens an Hour Earlier on Fridays and Saturdays
moreNews.body: Stonestown Galleria announced in late August that it is extending its hours, opening at 10 a.m. on Fridays and Saturdays and closing at 9 p.m. — one hour earlier than the previous 11 a.m. opening. Owner Brookfield Properties said the mall has had nearly no vacancies, and the schedule change reflects continued strong shopper and retailer interest. The San Francisco Chronicle reported the change on August 21, contrasting Stonestown's health with the still-shuttered San Francisco Centre downtown. The new hours took effect with the announcement.
